newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UN's Annan "hopeful" of peaceful Zaire transition.
newsitem.headline: UN's Annan "hopeful" of peaceful Zaire transition.

text.p: U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan said on Saturday he was "hopeful" that negotiators could avert a bloody conflict in Kinshasa and arrange a peaceful transition to democratic elections in Zaire.

He told a news conference during an official visit to Moscow: "We have not given up hope of getting the parties to accept some sort of a transitional arrangement and therefore avoid bloody conflict in the capital city, Kinshasa."

Annan said he also hoped mediators, who include United Nations special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun and senior South African officials, could convince rebel leader Laurent Kabila to form a coalition government before elections were held.

"I'm quite hopeful that we will be able to avoid bloodshed in Kinshasa and that we can convince Mr Kabila and the allies to form a broad-based government with other political elements participating in it.
"Once that is done, there will be time to prepare national elections," Annan said, stressing his hope that the "choice and the voice" of the Zairean people would be respected.
Kabila said on Saturday he was taking over as head of state with the agreement of generals in Kinshasa and he expected the capital to be in his hands in hours.
President Mobutu Sese Seko stepped aside and left Kinshasa on Friday, ending 32 years in power and leaving his emergency-rule government in charge of national policy.
